text:
What modifiers are implicitly applied to all interface methods?
(Choose all that apply)

answers.text: protected
public
static
void
abstract
default

correct.description: All interface methods are implicitly public, so option B is correct and option A is not[cite: 200]. Interface methods may be declared as static or default but are never implicitly added, so options C and F are incorrect[cite: 201]. Option D is incorrect—void is not a modifier; it is a return type[cite: 202]. Prior to Java 8 all interface methods would be assumed to be abstract[cite: 203]. Since Java 8 now includes default and static methods and they are never abstract, you cannot assume the abstract modifier will be implicitly applied to all methods by the compiler[cite: 204].

text:
Which of the following statements about polymorphism are true?
(Choose all that apply)

answers.text: A reference to an object may be cast to a subclass of the object without an explicit cast.
If a method takes a superclass of three objects, then any of those classes may be passed as a parameter to the method.
A method that takes a parameter with type java.lang.Object will take any reference.
All cast exceptions can be detected at compile-time.
By defining a public instance method in the superclass, you guarantee that the specific method will be called in the parent class at runtime.

correct.description: A reference to an object requires an explicit cast if referenced with a subclass, so option A is incorrect[cite: 226]. If the cast is to a superclass reference, then an explicit cast is not required[cite: 227]. Because of polymorphic parameters, if a method takes the superclass of an object as a parameter, then any subclass references may be used without a cast, so option B is correct[cite: 228]. All objects extend java.lang.Object, so if a method takes that type, any valid object, including null, may be passed; therefore, option C is correct[cite: 229, 230]. Some cast exceptions can be detected as errors at compile-time, but others can only be detected at runtime, so D is incorrect[cite: 230]. Due to the nature of polymorphism, a public instance method can be overridden in a subclass and calls to it will be replaced even in the superclass it was defined, so E is incorrect[cite: 231].

text:
Which statements are true for both abstract classes and interfaces?
(Choose all that apply)

answers.text: All methods within them are assumed to be abstract.
Both can contain public static final variables.
Both can be extended using the extend keyword.
Both can contain default methods.
Both can contain static methods.
Neither can be instantiated directly.
Both inherit java.lang.Object.

correct.description: Option A is wrong, because an abstract class may contain concrete methods[cite: 239]. Since Java 8, interfaces may also contain concrete methods in form of static or default methods[cite: 240]. Although all variables in interfaces are assumed to be public static final, abstract classes may contain them as well, so option B is correct[cite: 241]. Both abstract classes and interfaces can be extended with the extends keyword, so option C is correct[cite: 242]. Only interfaces can contain default methods, so option D is incorrect[cite: 243]. Both abstract classes and interfaces can contain static methods, so option E is correct[cite: 244]. Both structures require a concrete subclass to be instantiated, so option F is correct[cite: 245]. Finally, though an instance of an object that implements an interface inherits java.lang.Object, the interface itself doesn’t; otherwise, Java would support multiple inheritance for objects, which it doesn’t[cite: 246, 247].

text:
Which of the following is true about a concrete subclass?
(Choose all that apply)

answers.text: A concrete subclass can be declared as abstract.
A concrete subclass must implement all inherited abstract methods.
A concrete subclass must implement all methods defined in an inherited interface.
A concrete subclass cannot be marked as final.
Abstract methods cannot be overridden by a concrete subclass.

correct.description: Concrete classes are, by definition, not abstract, so option A is incorrect[cite: 263]. A concrete class must implement all inherited abstract methods, so option B is correct[cite: 264]. Option C is incorrect; a superclass may have already implemented an inherited interface, so the concrete subclass would not need to implement the method[cite: 265]. Concrete classes can be both final and not final, so option D is incorrect[cite: 266]. Finally, abstract methods must be overridden by a concrete subclass, so option E is incorrect[cite: 267].
